long_description: PRMS (Professional Risk Management Services) has been the American Psychiatric Association's endorsed professional liability insurance program since 1983. They exclusively serve psychiatrists and understand the unique liability risks of psychiatric practice, including medication management, involuntary commitment decisions, boundary issues, and forensic work. PRMS offers occurrence-based policies with limits up to $3M/$3M through A+ rated carriers. Their policies include coverage for telepsychiatry, ECT procedures, ketamine/esketamine treatment, collaborative care arrangements, and forensic psychiatry. PRMS is known for their psychiatric-specific risk management resources, including the acclaimed Psychiatrists' Program newsletter, risk management seminars, and access to expert consultation on liability questions. Their claims team has deep expertise in defending psychiatric malpractice cases. APA members receive preferred rates and additional benefits.

Yes, PRMS provides coverage for ketamine and esketamine (Spravato) treatment, which many general malpractice carriers exclude or require special endorsements for.

faqs.q: How much does psychiatrist malpractice insurance cost?
faqs.a: PRMS premiums for full-time psychiatrists typically range from $2,000-4,000/year for $1M/$3M coverage. Forensic work, ECT, and ketamine can significantly increase premiums.

faqs.q: Does PRMS cover forensic psychiatry and expert witness work?
faqs.a: Yes, PRMS offers specific coverage for forensic psychiatry including expert witness testimony, independent medical examinations, and custody evaluations.

faqs.q: Why is psychiatrist malpractice more expensive than therapist insurance?
faqs.a: Psychiatrists face higher liability due to prescribing medications, involuntary commitment decisions, ECT procedures, and other medical interventions that non-prescribers don't perform.
